chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The best of sacrificial animals (budn) are those with strong bloodlines (dhawat al-arham) among camels and cattle, and the male of the sacrificial animals and the stud/breeding male of sheep is sufficient (for sacrifice)."

key_terms.اَلْبُدْنِ: Sacrificial animals (specifically camels or large cattle used for sacrifice)
key_terms.ذَوَاتُ اَلْأَرْحَامِ: Those with strong bloodlines/lineage (literally 'possessors of wombs/uteri')

ai.seo_question: What are the best qualities for sacrificial animals in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* emphasizes the superiority of 'Dhawāt al-Arḥām' (animals with strong lineage or broad frames) for Udhiyah, reflecting the Shia scholarly preference for quality and robustness in sacrificial offerings. It further clarifies that while males are sufficient for both large livestock and sheep, the emphasis remains on selecting the best available specimen to honor the ritual. This ruling underscores the importance of intention and physical excellence in fulfilling the obligation of sacrifice.
